verdicts.reason: A keeps the original centered composition and reading order (logo, can, headline, CTA, legal), but it is essentially a scaled copy: the can is small, there is a dead gap between the can and the headline, the headline runs close to the edges and the sticker floats arbitrarily at top right. B moves the logo to the right, off the centered axis. It also jams the sticker placeholder directly under the CTA beside the tiny legal line, so the bottom is cramped while the middle is loose.

A has a clean centered stack with a strong two-line headline, but the logo is shrunk to a near-trivial size and the sticker sits awkwardly beside the legal text. B moves the logo off-axis to the right, against a centered layout. Its oversized CTA leaves almost no gap above the sticker, which crowds the bottom edge next to unreadably small legal text.

A right-aligns the logo against the centered axis and crams the sticker against the oversized CTA's bottom edge, with legal text jammed beside it. B keeps the centered logo and gives the CTA and footer more even spacing, though its logo is small and the sticker is still an arbitrary afterthought next to the legal line.

A is a balanced centered stack with clear hierarchy, though the logo is undersized and the sticker sits awkwardly in the footer. B keeps the original can-over-headline order, but the logo is right-aligned off-axis and the headline, CTA and sticker are packed into the lower third with almost no spacing. That leaves empty space at the top and a crowded bottom edge.
